title: Ais kacang (Singapore shaved ice with sweet toppings)
steps: Put the red beans, sweet corn, grass jelly and attap seeds into four bowls.
Pile the shaved ice over them into mounds.
Drizzle with rose syrup and gula melaka syrup.
Pour the evaporated milk over the ice and serve immediately.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Banmian (Singapore handmade flat noodles in anchovy soup)
steps: Mix the flour, egg and water into a dough, knead until smooth and rest for 30 minutes.
Simmer the anchovies in the water for 20 minutes, strain, and season with soy sauce.
Roll the dough thin and tear or cut it into rough flat strips.
Fry the pork with a little soy sauce until cooked.
Boil the noodles in the broth for 3 to 4 minutes, adding the greens for the last minute.
Serve with the pork, eggs and fried shallots with chili sauce on the side.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Black pepper crab (Singapore crab stir-fried with black pepper butter sauce)

ingredients.name: cleaned crab, cut into pieces and claws cracked

steps: Pat the crab dry.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a wok and fry the garlic and shallots until golden.
Add the black pepper and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the crab and toss for 2 minutes over high heat.
Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and water, cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once.
Stir in the remaining butter and spring onions, and serve.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Bubur cha cha (Singapore sweet potato and coconut dessert)
steps: Steam or boil the sweet potato and taro until just tender and set aside.
Cook the sago in plenty of boiling water until nearly transparent, then rinse in cold water and drain.
Heat the coconut milk, water, sugar, pandan leaves and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Add the sweet potato, taro and sago and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the banana at the end.
Serve warm or chilled.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Char kway teow (Singapore stir-fried flat rice noodles)
steps: Separate the noodles gently so they don't clump.
Heat the wok until very hot, add the oil and fry the garlic and sausage for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns and chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and both soy sauces and toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Push the noodles aside, scramble the eggs in the gap and mix in.
Add the bean sprouts and chives and toss for 30 seconds, then serve immediately.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chilli crab (Singapore crab in sweet and spicy egg-tomato sauce)

ingredients.name: cleaned mud or Dungeness crab, cut into pieces and claws cracked

steps: Buy the crab already killed, cleaned and cut or thaw frozen crab fully, and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the garlic, ginger and chilies until fragrant.
Stir in the ketchup, chili sauce, sugar, soy sauce and water and bring to a simmer.
Add the crab pieces, cover and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the shells are bright red and the meat opaque.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture to thicken, then drizzle in the beaten egg while stirring slowly to make ribbons.
Garnish with coriander and serve with warm buns for mopping up the sauce.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chwee kueh (Singapore steamed rice cakes with preserved radish)
steps: Whisk the flour, starch, salt and half the water until smooth.
Boil the remaining water and pour it into the batter in a stream, stirring, then cook briefly over low heat until slightly thickened.
Divide among small, oiled heatproof cups.
Steam for 15 to 20 minutes until the cakes are set and glossy, then cool completely so they firm up.
Fry the garlic and preserved radish with the sugar and soy sauce until fragrant and slightly crisp.
Unmould the cakes and top with the radish, adding chili sauce on the side.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Curry puff (Singapore flaky pastry with curried potato)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt, then add water and bring together into a dough. Rest for 30 minutes.
Fry the onion in oil, add the curry powder and chicken, then the potatoes, and cook until dry and thick. Cool completely.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 10 cm circles.
Put a spoonful of filling on each, fold into half-moons and crimp the edges firmly.
Brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden, or deep-fry at 170°C for 5 minutes.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Devil's curry (Kristang Eurasian chicken and potato curry)
steps: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric and lemongrass into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil for 8 to 10 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the mustard and chicken and stir to coat well.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes and water and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, sugar and salt and cook uncovered for 10 minutes to reduce the gravy, then serve with rice or bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Duck rice (Singapore Teochew braised duck with rice)
steps: Combine the soy sauces, sugar, spices, galangal, garlic and water in a pot large enough for the duck and bring to a boil.
Lower in the duck, breast side down, spoon the sauce over it and cover.
Simmer gently for 1 to 1.5 hours, turning halfway, until the meat is tender.
Add the eggs for the last 15 minutes.
Rest and carve the duck, spooning some of the braising liquid over rice, and serve with egg, cucumber and the sauce.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Fish head curry (Singapore sour and spicy fish curry with vegetables)

ingredients.name: red snapper or sea bream head, about 700 g, split and cleaned (or thick fish steaks)

steps: Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and curry leaves and fry until the seeds pop.
Add the shallots and garlic and fry until softened.
Mix the curry powder with a little water to a paste, add it and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the water, coconut milk, tamarind and salt and bring to a simmer.
Add the eggplant and okra and cook for 5 minutes.
Lay in the fish and tomatoes, cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes until the fish is cooked, then serve with rice.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Fish soup bee hoon (Singapore fish and vermicelli soup)
steps: Simmer the stock with the ginger for 10 minutes.
Season the fish with salt and pepper and flash-fry or sear it briefly if you like a richer broth.
Add the wine and soy sauce to the stock, add the fish and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until cooked.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft, drain and place in bowls.
Add the greens to the soup for 1 minute.
Ladle over the noodles, add the evaporated milk if using, and finish with pepper, shallots and coriander.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Hainanese chicken rice (poached chicken with fragrant rice)
steps: Rub the chicken inside and out with salt, and stuff the cavity with a few slices of ginger and a spring onion.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the remaining ginger and spring onions, lower in the chicken, return to a gentle simmer, then cover and turn off the heat. Leave for 40 minutes, until the thickest part is cooked through.
Plunge the chicken into iced water for 10 minutes to firm the skin, then drain, rub with sesame oil and rest. Keep the poaching stock.
Fry the garlic in the chicken fat until golden, add the rinsed rice and stir for 2 minutes, then cook in 600 ml of the stock until tender.
For the ginger sauce, mix the grated ginger with salt and hot oil. For the chili sauce, blend the chili sauce with the lime juice and a ladle of stock.
Carve the chicken and serve over the rice with cucumber, both sauces, soy sauce and a small bowl of the hot stock.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Hainanese curry rice (Singapore pork cutlet with curry gravy)
steps: Flatten the pork chops, season with salt and pepper and crumb them with flour, egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry the onion and garlic in a little oil, add the curry powder and fry for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, carrot, coconut milk, water and fish sauce and simmer for 20 minutes until soft and thick.
Fry the pork chops at 170°C until golden, about 4 minutes per side.
Slice the pork, put it on the rice and ladle the curry gravy over the top.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Ham chim peng (Singapore fried sweet dough with five-spice)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, baking powder, salt and five-spice powder.
Add the water and oil to make a soft dough and knead briefly.
Let it rise in a covered bowl for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces, roll each flat into a thin round, and let rest 10 minutes.
Deep-fry at 170°C for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain and sprinkle with sugar if desired.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Har cheong gai (Singapore prawn paste fried chicken wings)
steps: Mix the prawn paste with the sugar, wine and ginger.
Coat the wings in the paste and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Mix the cornstarch and flour and dust the wings with it.
Fry at 170°C for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through and golden.
Raise the heat and fry again for 1 minute for crispness, then drain and serve with lime.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Katong laksa (Singapore coconut curry noodle soup)

ingredients.name: thick rice vermicelli, cut into short lengths
prawn stock (made from the shells) or chicken stock

steps: Fry the laksa paste and ground dried shrimp in a little oil for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the prawn stock and bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar and warm through without a hard boil.
Poach the prawns in the broth for 2 minutes and lift them out.
Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts in hot water and divide into bowls, and cut the noodles with scissors if long.
Ladle the broth over, top with prawns, fish cake, egg, laksa leaves and a spoonful of sambal.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kaya toast (Singapore coconut jam toast with butter)
steps: Toast the bread over a griddle or in a toaster until golden and crisp on both sides.
Spread kaya generously on one slice of each pair.
Lay thin slices of cold butter over the kaya and cover with the second slice.
Cut into rectangles.
Crack the soft-boiled eggs into a bowl, season with soy sauce and pepper, and serve alongside for dipping.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kueh tutu (Singapore steamed rice flour cakes with peanut or coconut filling)

ingredients.name: desiccated coconut, steamed with 1 tbsp sugar

steps: Mix the flour, starch and salt with the water, rubbing between your fingers into damp crumbs, then sift for a fine texture.
Mix the peanuts with the sugar for one filling.
Oil small moulds and fill them with a thin layer of the damp flour.
Add a spoonful of filling and cover with more flour, pressing lightly.
Steam over high heat for 5 to 7 minutes until translucent and cooked.
Unmould and serve hot with coconut.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Mee rebus (Singapore noodles in sweet potato gravy)

ingredients.measure: fried shallots, green chilies, spring onion
ingredients.name: to garnish

steps: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, dried shrimp and soybean paste into a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil until fragrant and darker.
Mash the sweet potatoes with the water to make a thick liquid and add to the pan.
Add the sugar and salt and simmer for 20 minutes into a thick gravy.
Blanch the noodles and bean sprouts and divide into bowls.
Pour the hot gravy over and top with tofu, egg, fried shallots, chilies, spring onion and a squeeze of lime.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Mee siam (Singapore spicy-sour rice vermicelli)
steps: Blend the chilies, shallots, soybean paste and dried shrimp into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the water, tamarind liquid, sugar and salt and simmer for 10 minutes to make a gravy.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft and drain.
Toss the noodles in the gravy until coated, or serve the gravy poured over.
Top with bean sprouts, egg, chives and lime.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Ngoh hiang (Singapore five-spice pork and prawn rolls)

ingredients.name: dried bean curd skin, softened and cut in squares

steps: Mix the pork, prawns, carrot, water chestnuts, spring onions, five-spice powder, soy sauce, cornstarch and pepper until the mixture is well bound.
Place a line of filling along one edge of each bean curd sheet and roll up tightly, tucking in the ends.
Steam the rolls for 12 to 15 minutes until firm, then let them cool and dry.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry the rolls until golden brown and crisp.
Slice into pieces and serve with sweet chili sauce.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Popiah (Singapore fresh spring rolls)

ingredients.name: firm tofu or Chinese sausage, diced
eggs, scrambled into thin omelettes, sliced
sweet flour sauce (tim cheong) or hoisin

steps: Fry half the garlic in the oil, add the jicama and carrot with the soy sauce, cover and cook for 15 minutes until soft and moist.
Add the prawns and tofu and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Mix the remaining garlic with the sweet sauce and chili sauce.
Lay a wrapper flat, smear sauce down the middle and add lettuce, egg, a spoonful of filling and peanuts.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Cut in pieces and serve immediately.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Rojak (Singapore fruit and vegetable salad with prawn paste sauce)
steps: Mix the petis, sugar, tamarind, lime juice and chili paste into a thick, dark sauce.
Toss the pineapple, cucumber, jicama, bean sprouts and tofu with the sauce.
Add the youtiao and half the peanuts and toss quickly.
Sprinkle with the remaining peanuts and serve at once.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Sambal stingray (Singapore grilled stingray with sambal on banana leaf)

ingredients.name: stingray wing or skate wing, cut into portions

steps: Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic and toasted belacan into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil for 8 minutes until darker and fragrant, then add sugar, tamarind and salt.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame, lay the fish on them and spread a thick layer of sambal on top.
Wrap or fold up the sides and grill or bake at 220°C for 12 to 15 minutes until the fish is opaque and flaky.
Serve on the leaf with lime wedges.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Satay bee hoon (Singapore rice vermicelli with peanut sauce)
steps: Blend the chilies and shallots to a paste and fry it in the oil until fragrant.
Add the crushed peanuts, sugar and tamarind water along with 200 ml of water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the vermicelli until tender, drain and blanch the bean sprouts.
Place noodles in bowls with spinach, bean sprouts, cucumber and meat.
Spoon the hot peanut sauce over the top and serve.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Singapore bak kut teh (peppery pork rib soup)

ingredients.name: pork ribs, cut into short pieces
garlic bulbs, left whole, tops trimmed

ingredients.measure: youtiao, rice and chilies in soy sauce
ingredients.name: to serve

steps: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Place the ribs in a clean pot with the whole garlic, peppercorns and water.
Bring to a boil, skim, then cover and simmer for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and the broth is pepper-spiced.
Add the soy sauces and salt and simmer for 10 more minutes.
Serve in bowls with rice, fried dough sticks and chilies in dark soy sauce on the side.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Singapore Hokkien mee (stir-fried prawn noodles)
steps: Simmer the prawn shells in water for 15 minutes and strain to make a stock.
Fry the garlic in oil, push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the noodles and vermicelli with the stock, oyster sauce, soy sauce and fish sauce.
Cook, tossing, for 4 to 5 minutes until the stock is mostly absorbed and the noodles tender.
Add the prawns, squid and bean sprouts and cook 2 more minutes.
Serve with spring onions, lime wedges and sambal.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Vegetarian bee hoon (Singapore fried rice vermicelli)

ingredients.name: dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced

steps: Soak the vermicelli in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Fry the garlic and mushrooms in the oil until fragrant.
Add the carrot, cabbage and tofu and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the soy sauces and mushroom liquid and bring to a simmer.
Add the vermicelli and toss until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are tender.
Season with white pepper and top with spring onions.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Yong tau foo (Singapore stuffed tofu and vegetables in broth)

ingredients.name: firm tofu squares, halved to make pockets

ingredients.measure: sweet bean sauce and chili sauce
ingredients.name: to dip

steps: Mix the minced fish with the cornstarch, salt, pepper and sesame oil and beat for a minute until it is springy and sticky.
Fill the tofu pockets, okra and pepper halves with a spoonful of paste, smoothing the surface.
Simmer the stock with the soy sauce.
Poach the stuffed pieces in the stock for 6 to 8 minutes until the filling is firm.
Serve in bowls with the broth, with sweet bean sauce and chili sauce for dipping.
